newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmakers reject 'No Budget, No Pay' bill.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmakers reject 'No Budget, No Pay' bill.

text.p: California legislators on Friday rejected a bill that would require state lawmakers to give up their pay if they are late enacting the state's budget.
The bill failed to muster the majority it needed to clear the state Assembly Budget Committee. As a result, the proposal could not advance to the Assembly floor, lawmakers said.

The measure, dubbed the "No Budget, No Pay!" bill, would have required the governor and legislators to forfeit their pay for each day that they are late enacting the state budget. Legislators would also forfeit the $105 per diem they receive for daily expenses.
Republican Assemblyman Jim Morrissey, who introduced the bill, said his proposal would have provided a strong incentive to lawmakers to finalize the state's budget on time.

The legislature is required to approve the state budget no later than June 15, and it must be signed by the governor no later than June 30. But the governor and the legislature have regularly failed to meet the July 1 deadline. In 1992, the budget was more than two months late.
A similar bill failed last year.
